values.value: • Convert confidence into a concrete close plan rather than optimism. • List what remains, who owns each item, and the exact dates tied to closure. • Validate that your confidence is backed by buyer signals, not only internal hope. • Keep pressure light but disciplined through the final stretch. • Use confidence to drive execution, not complacency.
20|Yes
Buyer may say, 'Sounds promising, but let us see.' Response: 'Absolutely. I want to back my confidence with a clear action plan so both sides know exactly what closes this.'
Good. Convert confidence into a dated action plan so confidence becomes execution, not optimism.
Low risk. Finish with discipline.
Ask: 'What are the final steps we should lock today to land this inside the timeline?'
Yes

• Identify what is blocking full confidence and tackle that directly. • Check for buyer access gaps, budget uncertainty, competition, legal steps, or unresolved objections. • Turn vague concern into a named risk with an owner and next action. • Use the dashboard signals to decide whether to reopen discovery, tighten close plan, or hold proposal. • Forecast with discipline until confidence is earned.
20|Partially confident
Buyer may say, 'There are still a few open concerns.' Response: 'That is helpful. Let us name those concerns directly so we can close them one by one.'
List exactly what still worries you, then remove those issues one by one. Confidence improves through control.
Risk: Moderate slippage risk.
Ask: 'What are the top two reasons this may still slip, and how do we handle them now?'
Partially confident

• Do not hide the weak confidence behind activity. • Name the top reasons this deal may slip or be lost. • Take one corrective action on each major risk instead of sending more generic follow-ups. • If the core gaps are not fixable, reduce forecast weight and refocus effort. • Low confidence should trigger honest deal repair, not hopeful chasing.
20|Not confident
Buyer may say, 'We are unsure this will move soon.' Response: 'Understood. Then I would rather diagnose the real blockers now than keep pushing generic follow-ups.'
Do not hide your own doubt. Re-qualify the deal and fix the biggest blocker before spending more effort.
High risk: Seller confidence is weak for a reason.
Say: 'I want to be honest. Before we push ahead, we need to solve the main blocker first.'
Not confident

• Your forecast quality is weak because the current signals are unclear. • Audit the deal: problem, urgency, buyer access, process, budget, competition, and next step. • Use that review to decide whether this is a real opportunity or only an active conversation. • Rebuild confidence from facts, not intuition. • Only then commit to an internal close view.
20|Don't know
Buyer may say, 'Too early to tell.' Response: 'Fair enough. Let us do a quick deal audit together so the next steps are based on facts, not guesses.'
Pause and review the deal end to end. If you cannot explain how this closes, the buyer probably cannot either.
High risk: No close path clarity.
Ask: 'What exact event, person, or gap is stopping me from seeing a clear close path?'
Don't know
Are you fully confident of getting this deal within the proposed timeline ?
